title: Constant outer terms: a trivialising cover for the middle term
statement: Let X be a scheme, Λ a finite (not necessarily commutative) ring, and 0 → F₁ → E → F₃ → 0 a short exact sequence of sheaves of left Λ-modules on the small étale site of X [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Assume F₁ and F₃ are constant [def-constructible-constant] and have finitely generated geometric stalks [def-constructible-finite]. There exists an étale cover (Uᵢ → X) such that the inverse image of E on every Uᵢ is a constant sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03RX (3), lemma-kernel-finite-locally-constant; via Modules on Sites Tag 093U

proof.text: On a nonempty scheme, identify the constant values M and N with geometric stalks, so they are finitely generated by the finite-sheaf definition. Choose finitely many generators of N and their presentation Λ^m → N with kernel K. Since Λ is finite, Λ^m and K are finite.

Use local surjectivity of the epimorphism E → N_X to lift each chosen generator. Intersect the finitely many covering sieves to lift all generators on one cover; these define a map r:(Λ^m)_U → E|_U lifting the presentation map. This is the local lift statement, here required for Ring Λ and ModuleCat-valued sheaves rather than its present commutative SheafOfModules specialization.

The constant presentation sequence remains exact. The restriction of r to K factors through M_U as g. The map M_U ⊞ (Λ^m)_U → E|_U induced by the injection and r is epi: its image contains M_U and maps onto N_U. Its kernel is the image of (-g,inclusion): K_U → M_U ⊞ (Λ^m)_U, by the chase a+r(v)=0 ⇒ q(v)=0 ⇒ v=k∈K ⇒ a=-g(k). Thus its cokernel is E|_U.

The direct sum is constant, and the morphism from finite K_U to it is locally induced by a module map. The constant-morphism lemma identifies its cokernel with the constant sheaf of the module cokernel on a further cover. Bind the covers; for an empty scheme the empty cover suffices.
